## When to use it

Use this template after the expectations conversation to record the working arrangement. Review it after the first 90 days, after a major project change and whenever the supervisory team changes. Complete any mandatory institutional form separately.

## Blank agreement

**Purpose and scope:**
[What this agreement covers and which formal policy sits above it.]

**Supervisory team and roles:**
[Name roles, not private personal information in a public copy.]

**Decision authority:**
[Student provisional decisions; whole-team decisions; formal or specialist decisions.]

**Meeting cadence and preparation:**
[Frequency, agenda timing, papers and cancellation arrangements.]

**Communication and urgency:**
[Routine channel, urgent route, reasonable boundaries.]

**Feedback:**
[Reviewable material, requested focus, ordinary turnaround, long-work arrangements.]

**Records:**
[Who records decisions and actions, where they are stored, correction window.]

**Continuity and absence:**
[How planned and unexpected absence will be handled.]

**Development and independence:**
[Priority skills, networks, decision responsibilities and review of progress.]

**Authorship and contributions:**
[When and how contribution expectations will be recorded and revisited.]

**Concerns and escalation:**
[Current independent support and formal routes; do not include sensitive case details.]

**Review date:**
[Date and trigger events.]

**Acknowledgement:**
[How participants confirm that the record reflects the discussion.]

## Completed example

**Purpose and scope:** This record describes ordinary working arrangements. Current course rules and institutional policy take priority.

**Team and authority:** The student prepares recommendations and may make reversible operational choices. Changes to the central question or design are discussed with both supervisors. Ethics and candidature decisions use the formal institutional process.

**Meetings and feedback:** Fortnightly meetings for the first 90 days. Agenda and papers arrive two working days before. Short review requests ordinarily receive a response within ten working days; longer work is scheduled.

**Records:** The student circulates decisions, actions and unresolved questions within two working days. Supervisors correct factual errors within five working days. Silence is not recorded as formal approval.

**Continuity:** Planned absence longer than two weeks is recorded in advance with a nominated contact and any milestone effect.

**Development:** The student leads agenda preparation and presents a recommendation for major decisions. The arrangement is reviewed at day 90.

## Scenario test

**Situation:** A principal supervisor will be unavailable for six weeks immediately before a formal milestone.

**Use:** The continuity section prompts an early decision about review coverage, decision authority, revised timing and the graduate research contact. The absence does not remain a private scheduling surprise.

## Local checks

Confirm whether your institution requires a particular agreement, review schedule, minimum meeting frequency, supervisor workload allocation or formal approval for team changes.
